an4.77:1.1: “There are these four inconceivables that are not to be conjectured about, that would bring madness & vexation to anyone who conjectured about them.
an4.77:1.3: “The Buddha-range of the Buddhas [i.e., the range of powers a Buddha develops as a result of becoming a Buddha] is an inconceivable that is not to be conjectured about,
an4.77:1.4: that would bring madness & vexation to anyone who conjectured about it.
an4.77:1.5: “The jhāna-range of a person in jhāna [i.e, the range of powers that one may obtain while absorbed in jhāna].…
an4.77:1.7: “The [precise working out of the] results of kamma.…
an4.77:1.9: “Conjecture about [the origin, etc., of] the world is an inconceivable that is not to be conjectured about,
an4.77:1.10: that would bring madness & vexation to anyone who conjectured about it.
an4.77:1.11: “These are the four inconceivables that are not to be conjectured about, that would bring madness & vexation to anyone who conjectured about them.”
